Header: Cnaphalocrocis medinalis Rice leaf folder; rice leaf roller

Prevention: Rice leaf folder is a species of moth which causes most damage as a larva (caterpillar).
If high infestation occurred in previous season, plough the land just after harvesting.
Use recommended seed rate i.e. 40 to 50 kg per acre.
Avoid close planting; leave 30 cm space every 2.5 m.
This will help minimise the build up of humid conditions favoured by the pest.
Avoid excess use of nitrogen fertilizer as this can increase the susceptibility of plants to infestation.
Ask extension worker for a recommended rate.
If the area is prone to infestation, remove grassy weeds in crop and surroundings.
Grassy weeds act as alternative host plants.
Avoid broad spectrum pesticides and unnecessary pesticide application to conserve natural enemies such as parasitic wasps, predatory beetles, spiders and predatory crickets ( Anaxipha spp.)
Place bamboo tops or twigs for perching of predatory birds soon after planting.
However, remove these at flowering stage of the crop.
Monitoring: Observe the field at least once a week for leaf folder damage, from tillering to flowering.
Folded, with the edges of leaves joined by a fine white silk.
Larva are often found inside the folded leaves.
Longitudinal, white, transparent streaks on the leaf blades (larvae feeding damage)
Larva: 12-25 mm long, white with a brown head when newly hatched, turning light green when they begin feeding and pinkish yellow when fully grown
Form inside the folded leaf or further down in a sheath near the stem base.
Adult moth: 8-12 mm long, 16 mm wingspan, dark brown margin on the wings and three brown stripes in the centre, the middle one of which is shorter than the others.
If infestation is heavy then patches of the field may appear scorched.
Young and green rice plants tend to be most severely infested.
Use sweep nets and light traps to monitor for moths.
Direct Control: When infestation is low/damage first appears in patches, remove the damaged leaves along with larvae and manually destroy or burn.
